BijakAttemptStatus.description: in_progress = open; submitted = handed in by the student; auto_submitted = closed by the client at zero time or by the server sweeper after deadline + grace ("Dihantar automatik"); abandoned = discarded or replaced by a restart ("Ditinggalkan").

key.description: Opaque photo key issued by the upload route (the mock used a device-local IndexedDB key). The server only accepts keys it issued for this attempt and part.

choice.description: MCQ option id, or a letter for match_letter.

plain.description: Plain-text forms of steps and final.

rev.description: Per-part revision: a save with a revision not above the stored one never overwrites.

partId.description: Leaf part id (for an MCQ question the question id). A part that is not on the attempt, or is locked (latihan after the check cap), is ignored.

savedAt.description: Device time of the last edit. Never trusted: the server stores min(savedAt, server now), and for a late sync a change counts only when that value is at or before the deadline.

flags.description: Flagged question ids; replaces the stored list when present.

picks.description: Choose-N picks per section id (ticked question ids); replaces the stored map when present.

answers.description: The device full answer set per part id (AC-13.2); merged with `changes`, and the server grades the union of what it saved and what the request carries.

auto.description: True when the client submits at zero time (status auto_submitted).

restart.description: True: every open attempt of the caller on this paper becomes abandoned and a new one starts (AC-12.2). Absent or false: the most recent open attempt is returned.

elapsedSeconds.description: Server now minus startedAt, in whole seconds.

paperKind.description: pilihan = curated paper, jana = paper generated for the caller.

deadline.description: startedAt + durationMin, computed from the server clock at start (AC-05.1); null in latihan. The client clock never moves it.

answers.description: The caller own saved answers per part id.

checked.description: Latihan: question ids already checked with "Semak".

checkCounts.description: Latihan: "Semak" count per question id, capped at 3.

lateBySeconds.description: Seconds past the deadline at submit (a sweep close is capped at 300). Absent when on time.

ecf.description: Set when an own-figure-carried-forward mark was given.

counted.description: False when a choose-N section dropped this question from the total.

checks.description: Latihan, in progress: the per-question results (scheme revealed) of the questions already checked. Always empty in exam mode and for a closed attempt.

BijakBuilderSectionRule.description: { type: all } = answer every question; { type: choose, n } = answer n of the questions (choose-N counts only the N largest questions in the section marks).

BijakBuilderPaperStatus.description: draf = being assembled (editable, can be deleted); terbit = published, visible in Kertas Pilihan and locked. Unpublish (tarik balik) sets the status back to draf; there is no ready or withdrawn state. Mapping to BE-15 `papers.status` (draft, ready, published, withdrawn) is internal: draf = draft or withdrawn, terbit = published; ready is not exposed.

BijakBuilderQuestionStatus.description: Question lifecycle code (D54a): draft, review, approved, published, archived. Prototype mapping: semakan = review, terbit = published, draf = draft (the prototype also reports draf for a question that is not in the bank); ditolak (rejected) has no D54 code and maps to draft, a contract choice [PROPOSED]. The builder offers only published questions as candidates (`getPaperEditor`: terbit, same subject and kertas); a paper can reference questions of any status, and publish refuses any that is not published ("{N} soalan belum Terbit").

Approved sets only: a draft, pending, archived or unknown set, a section number outside 1..4, or a section without audio is 404 "Not Found.". This is the `audioUrl` of the player data. Headers: `Content-Type` of the stored audio (audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/wav, audio/ogg), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. One `Range: bytes=a-b` is honoured with 206 and `Content-Range`; a range whose start is past the end is 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */size`; a malformed range (for example end before start) is ignored and the whole body is served with 200 (RFC 7233).

post.summary: Import questions from a CSV file
post.description: Admin only. multipart/form-data (file storage: BE-04). UTF-8, first row is the header (case-insensitive), comma separator, `"` quoting with `""`, quoted fields may span lines, blank lines ignored. Required columns question_text, option_a, option_b, correct_answer; correct_answer is a letter A to D (any case); subject_id, education_level_id and difficulty_level come from the row or the form default; marks default 1. Each valid row creates a `draft` question (it never bypasses review); a bad row is reported with its 1-based file line (header = line 1) and does not stop the others. The whole import is one transaction. An accepted file always answers 201. Flash: "Import selesai: <x> soalan diimport, <y> gagal.".

get.description:
Roles student and admin only; the data is always the session user's own. Any query parameter is ignored (no user parameter exists). No AI call, no stored copy: computed on every request.
Rules: (1) the caller's own answers that have a chapter are grouped by chapter id (never by name); answers without a chapter are not grouped. (2) A chapter is shown only with at least 5 attempts (HEATMAP_MIN_ATTEMPTS). (3) percent = floor((200 x correct + attempts) / (2 x attempts)), round half up. (4) band on the rounded percent: red < 50, amber 50..79, green >= 80. (5) Names come from the curriculum; a shown chapter whose chapter or subject is not found is skipped. (6) Topics inside a subject: raw accuracy ascending (exact integer cross-multiplication), then name ascending (code-unit comparison), then chapter id ascending (numeric). Subjects: curriculum order ascending, then subject id (numeric). (7) A subject with no shown chapter has no block; with none at all the body is { data: { subjects: [] } }.

200.description: Subjects with their shown topics; `subjects` is empty when no chapter reaches 5 attempts.

get.description: Mock GET /api/dashboard. One read model: greeting, trial, streak, wallet, this week (Monday-Sunday, Malaysia time), banners, today quests, badges, revision total, latest articles, subjects with counts, question-bank statistics, level pills, newest approved questions and per-subject stats. post.description:
Joins the quick-match queue and returns the queue id. Response is raw (un-enveloped, live-shaped).
The server first checks that 10 eligible keyless questions can be drawn; otherwise 422 with an empty body `{}`.
422 `{}` also covers an invalid question_type, subject, PKSK domain or level; 403 `{}` is an SPM request from a caller below Tingkatan 4. The BM texts (see BATTLE_MESSAGES) are NOT sent on these two routes (BR-M16-03).
Opponents are deterministic bots chosen by the server (D53(a)); real-time multiplayer is not part of this contract.

get.description:
Polled every 3 s by the owner. Only the owner sees the queue; anyone else gets `{status:"not_found"}` with HTTP 200.
The first two polls answer `waiting`, the third matches a bot and answers `matched` with the battle uuid; later polls repeat that answer. A queue older than 120 s, or not polled for more than 10 s, answers `expired`.
A pending join request turns the queue into `incoming_challenge`, with the challenger name, grade label and school (no id).
The 404 `{error:"Tiada lawan dijumpai."}` answers when no bot can be picked; the 422 `{error:"Soalan tidak mencukupi."}` when the 10 questions cannot be drawn at match time.

post.summary: Check one single-player answer (D58a) [PROPOSED route, not in the mock]
post.description: Modelled on the Bijak "Semak" check (/bijak/attempts/{id}/questions/{questionId}/check). Own session only. The path parameter `game` selects the body and the result: betul-salah = GamesBetulSalahCheck / GamesBetulSalahCheckResult, cabaran-kilat = GamesCabaranKilatCheck / GamesCabaranKilatCheckResult, tembak-jawapan = GamesTembakJawapanCheck / GamesTembakJawapanCheckResult, susun-jawapan = GamesSusunJawapanCheck / GamesSusunJawapanCheckResult, kad-memori = GamesKadMemoriCheck / GamesKadMemoriCheckResult (one named component each; request and response `examples` are keyed by game). A body of another game is 422. The server checks the answer against the stored key, stores the check, and returns correct/wrong plus the key of that item, revealed only now ({ data }). One check per item: a second check of the same item is 409 (so the key cannot be probed by retrying). Kad Memori: the body names two cards by opaque id; the response carries BOTH faces (the board never does), correct when they are a pair, and pair_id only on a match (null on a mismatch); a mismatch may be repeated, a card of an already matched pair is 409, and if another card is open (revealed, not checked) 409 "Sila padankan kad yang dibuka dahulu." [PROPOSED]. Every stored check feeds the final submit (moves = number of Kad Memori checks). Standard `{ error }` bodies. All BM texts of this route are [PROPOSED] (the mock has no check route): 404 "Sesi tidak dijumpai." and "Soalan tidak dijumpai." (copy reused from Jutawan), 409 "Soalan sudah dijawab.", "Kad sudah dipadankan.", 422 "Jawapan tidak sah." (reused). The response carries answer keys, so Cache-Control: no-store.

post.summary: Reveal one Kad Memori face (D58a) [PROPOSED route, LEAD decision pending]
post.description: The mock page shows the face of the first flipped card at once, so the first card of a move needs a reveal; the second card comes with the check response. Static path: wins over `/games/solo/{game}/...`. At most one card may be open (revealed and not yet checked). Revealing the card that is already open is idempotent: 200 with the same face, nothing changes (a client that lost the first response can reveal it again). Revealing a different card while one is open is 409 "Sila padankan kad yang dibuka dahulu." [PROPOSED], and the open card is closed by the next check naming it, so reveals never outnumber moves by more than one and the faces cannot be read without playing. A matched card is 409 "Kad sudah dipadankan." [PROPOSED]. If the LEAD prefers faces via the check response only, drop this route and the page shows the first card face-down until the second tap. Standard `{ error }` bodies; the face is not a key but is sent no-store.

post.summary: Apply for a foster family (Mohon Keluarga Angkat)
post.description: Any signed-in role (student, parent, teacher, admin). The applicant user id and role come from the session; applicantUserId or applicantRole in the body are ignored. The studentEmail must be the e-mail of an existing user with role student (surrounding spaces trimmed; letter case as the user lookup treats it). Inserts one application with status `pending` and createdAt = now. No duplicate check (the same student and applicant may apply again), no notification, no e-mail. Write-only: the category, income range and reason of a minor are never returned by any route and never logged. The success text "Permohonan anda telah dihantar. Admin akan menyemak permohonan dalam 1-3 hari bekerja." is shown by the client, not returned. Security note (OQ-API-B4-20): the studentEmail 422 tells a signed-in caller whether an e-mail belongs to a student, so the route is rate limited (RATE_LIMITED 429 with retryAfter and Retry-After, D57(a), BE-33). post.description: Public. Roles are limited to student, teacher and parent (default student); any other role in the body is a 422. Student and parent: creates an active account and logs it in (the response is the contract Session and the session cookie is set, not remembered). Teacher (privacy: a teacher gets school scope, which reaches the data of children): created inactive, with no school and the requested school kept as pending, and NO session; the answer is {status: pending_verification, message}. Until a school_admin verifies the account (BE-21), login is 403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE. A teacher must give a schoolId (422 otherwise). A duplicate e-mail (case-insensitive) is a 422 on `fields.email`. Rate limit (BE-06 AC6, D57a): per client IP, the BE-03 login numbers: 5 failed attempts per 60 seconds, then 429 until the window ends with doubling backoff on repeat; only refused attempts (422) count, so legitimate registrations are not slowed. Status is 201 for both variants; narrow with the check status-in-data (present = pending, absent = Session). The response is Cache-Control: no-store. Accepted residual risk (security review, by design as the mock and the UX): the 422 emailTaken lets a client learn whether an e-mail is registered; it is bounded only by the per-IP limit above. Log redaction (BE-NFR-10, BE-NFR-11): the request body, the IC number, the reset token, the e-mail and every password are never written to application logs, audit rows or error bodies (an e-mail may appear only masked, a token only as its id).

201.description: Student or parent: registered and logged in (data is the Session, cookie set). Teacher: created INACTIVE with no school scope and no session until a school_admin verifies the account; data is {status: pending_verification, message} and no cookie is set.

post.description: Public. Answers 200 "We have emailed your password reset link." for a known AND an unknown e-mail alike (existence is never disclosed; approved deviation D55b from the mock 422 "We can't find a user with that email address.", card AC3). Token rules: The token is at least 128 bits from a CSPRNG; only its hash is stored; it is valid 60 minutes and single use; issuing a new token revokes every earlier unused token of that user (one active token); a successful reset consumes every outstanding token of the user; the stored hash is compared in constant time; an inactive account is never issued a token; a successful reset-ic and a successful reset notify the account owner AND the school (D59a, see ACCOUNT_SECURITY_NOTIFICATIONS); the token is bound to the e-mail it was issued for and is redeemable only with that same e-mail. The e-mailed link carries the token in the URL fragment (/password/reset#token=...&email=...), never in the path or query, so it is not sent to servers, logs or Referer; the reset pages send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. The mail goes through a MailPort; the dev MailPort logs only the masked e-mail and the token id, never the link or the token. Throttle (uniform, no enumeration): one request per 60 seconds per e-mail, keyed on the hash of the normalised e-mail for EVERY request whether the e-mail exists, is inactive or not (the state of an unknown e-mail is stored too, bounded by expiry); every reset-ic attempt (match or not) starts the same 60 second throttle, so a 429 here is never a match oracle. A second request inside the interval is 429 RATE_LIMITED with retryAfter and the Retry-After header; in addition 20 requests per client IP per 60 seconds across all e-mails. Do the same work for known and unknown e-mails (no timing difference). Log redaction (BE-NFR-10, BE-NFR-11): the request body, the IC number, the reset token, the e-mail and every password are never written to application logs, audit rows or error bodies (an e-mail may appear only masked, a token only as its id).

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description: Public. Replaces the password, consumes the token (single use) and invalidates the user's other sessions (card AC2), then logs the user in: the response is the contract Session plus the flash text, and the cookie is set (not remembered). An unknown, used, expired or other-e-mail token, and an unknown e-mail, all answer 422 "This password reset token is invalid." on fields.email: the unknown e-mail never gets a user-not-found message (decided, D55b, no account enumeration; the mock answered "We can't find a user with that email address."). An inactive account is refused with 403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE and nothing changes (reachable only with a valid token, so not an oracle). Token rules: The token is at least 128 bits from a CSPRNG; only its hash is stored; it is valid 60 minutes and single use; issuing a new token revokes every earlier unused token of that user (one active token); a successful reset consumes every outstanding token of the user; the stored hash is compared in constant time; an inactive account is never issued a token; a successful reset-ic and a successful reset notify the account owner AND the school (D59a, see ACCOUNT_SECURITY_NOTIFICATIONS); the token is bound to the e-mail it was issued for and is redeemable only with that same e-mail. Every wrong redemption counts as a failure: 5 failures per 60 seconds per (e-mail hash, client IP) and 20 per client IP, then 429 RATE_LIMITED with retryAfter and the Retry-After header (BE-03 login numbers, backoff doubling). A successful reset: invalidates the user's other sessions and remember tokens, re-hashes the password with argon2id, clears must-change-password, writes an audit event (without the token) and notifies the user in-app (proposed copy "Kata laluan telah ditetapkan semula") and the school admins of the user's school (D59a, proposed copy "Kata laluan murid ditetapkan semula"; none for an account without a school). The response sets the session cookie and is Cache-Control: no-store. Log redaction (BE-NFR-10, BE-NFR-11): the request body, the IC number, the reset token, the e-mail and every password are never written to application logs, audit rows or error bodies (an e-mail may appear only masked, a token only as its id).

post.summary: Reset by e-mail and IC number (returns a reset token)
post.description: Public. The IC number is compared with its stored hash and is never returned. A match returns a reset token (data.token only, the e-mail is not echoed) bound to that e-mail: it can only be redeemed through /auth/password/reset together with the same e-mail, never for another account or any other way. Token rules: The token is at least 128 bits from a CSPRNG; only its hash is stored; it is valid 60 minutes and single use; issuing a new token revokes every earlier unused token of that user (one active token); a successful reset consumes every outstanding token of the user; the stored hash is compared in constant time; an inactive account is never issued a token; a successful reset-ic and a successful reset notify the account owner AND the school (D59a, see ACCOUNT_SECURITY_NOTIFICATIONS); the token is bound to the e-mail it was issued for and is redeemable only with that same e-mail. The response is Cache-Control: no-store. An unknown e-mail, an inactive account, an account without a stored IC (teacher, parent) and a wrong IC number are indistinguishable in status, body and timing (equal work, dummy compare; no token is issued for an inactive account): 422 "Email atau No Kad Pengenalan tidak sepadan." on fields.email. A match behaves no differently from a miss for throttling: EVERY attempt, match or not, also starts the 60 second per-e-mail throttle of /auth/password/email (keyed on the e-mail hash), so a 429 there never reveals a correct guess. A match is audited (without the IC or the token) and notifies the account owner AND the school in-app (NotificationsService.push: the owner, proposed copy "Permintaan tetap semula kata laluan", and the school admins of the user's school, proposed copy "Kata laluan murid ditetapkan semula" naming the user by display name only; an account without a school notifies only its owner), so a takeover is visible. Decided D59a: IC-only reset is allowed for all roles including pupils, with D55a limits and owner + school notification. Log redaction (BE-NFR-10, BE-NFR-11): the request body, the IC number, the reset token, the e-mail and every password are never written to application logs, audit rows or error bodies (an e-mail may appear only masked, a token only as its id). Attempt limit (D55a): at most 5 attempts per 15 minutes, counted separately per account (e-mail, whether or not it exists, so the limit does not reveal existence) and per client IP; every attempt counts, successful or not, and whichever limit is reached first answers 429 RATE_LIMITED with retryAfter seconds (also the Retry-After header).

post.description: Creates an active pupil of the caller school (createdBy = the caller); with classId the pupil is enrolled with source school_admin. D55c: the response shows the password once, to the creating admin only (never logged, never stored in plain text, not retrievable again) and returns mustChangePassword false (R39): the account is not flagged, so the first login does not force a password change; the pupil can change it in /profile/edit. The 201 carries Cache-Control: no-store (D57b). LOST RESPONSE: the credential is never re-served. If the 201 is lost, a retry answers 422 "The email has already been taken." and the password is gone; recover with POST /admin-sekolah/pelajar/{id}/reset-password (the admin sets a new password). The server must not store the plaintext to support a retry. The optional Idempotency-Key header prevents a duplicate account on a retry: a replayed key answers 409 CONFLICT and never re-serves the credential. ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF (e-mail enumeration): the e-mail is unique across all schools, so the 422 "The email has already been taken." reveals that an address is registered somewhere (a pupil of another school included). It cannot be hidden without dropping uniqueness; it is mitigated by the 429 rate limit and the audit trail. D59b: there is no password in the request and no shared default password: the server ALWAYS generates a random initial password (CSPRNG, at least 12 characters; exact policy in the implementation card) and returns it once in credential.password with mustChangePassword false (R39). Mass assignment waiver: role, schoolId, isActive, grade, icNumber and a password key in the body are ignored, never bound (BE-NFR-05 exception, mock fidelity). 429 RATE_LIMITED guards bulk account creation.

get.description: Roles in B1: admin, school_admin, teacher (student, parent, sponsor and ppd_officer get 403). School access: admin any school; school_admin its own school; teacher its own school or a school of a class it owns. A school outside the caller reach answers 404 NOT_FOUND "Not Found.", indistinguishable from an unknown school (BE-NFR-05, no school-id enumeration); 403 is only for a role that is not allowed. PDPA: the pupil lists show minors' names, classes and risk scores; never cache them and show them only to staff who need them. Risk is computed at request time and never stored: per pupil A = 100 - mean practice accuracy, E = min(100, days since active x 100 / 30), M = (10 - mean mastery) x 10, score = 0.4A + 0.3E + 0.3M (1 decimal). The role is checked first (403); then an unknown school and a school outside the caller scope are both 404 (the mock answered 403 for the latter; changed so the 403/404 difference cannot be used to list valid school ids).

get.description: Roles: admin (any school) and school_admin (own school); a teacher or any other role gets 403. Check order: the role check (403) comes BEFORE the 404; then an unknown school and a school outside the caller scope are both 404 (indistinguishable; the mock answered 403 for the latter). File name amaran-sekolah-{id}-{yyyymmdd}.csv (date in Malaysia time). Headers: Content-Type text/csv; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control no-store. Body: UTF-8 BOM, CRLF line ends with a trailing CRLF; header Bil,Pelajar,Tingkatan / Kelas,Skor Risiko,Status,Ketepatan,Penglibatan,Penguasaan; one line per pupil of the school (no tingkatan filter), score with one decimal, status label, then the three BM cell texts of the risk page. Cells starting with = + - @ tab or CR are prefixed with an apostrophe; quoting follows RFC 4180. No IC, e-mail or phone. PDPA: the file lists minors' names, classes and risk scores, the most sensitive derived data; it is never cached and rate limited (429, proposed on top of D57a because it is a bulk dump of minors). Every accepted download writes an audit event (actor, school, file name) and never personal content.

put.description: Body { title?, year?, durationMin?, sections?: [{ id, questionIds }] }; only the keys sent change. This one route carries every edit (the mock savePaper). A terbit paper is refused: 422 VALIDATION_ERROR "Kertas Terbit tidak boleh disunting. Tarik balik dahulu." (no field). Other refusals: title "Tajuk kertas diperlukan"; a section id that is not a section of the paper "Bahagian tidak sah"; a question id that does not exist, or whose curriculum subject differs from the paper subject, "Soalan tidak sah untuk kertas ini" (an existence and subject check only, not a kertas or status check). Duplicates and split groups are not refused here; they come back as publish errors. Answers the editor data (PaperEditorData), as the mock does. The mock throws error kind bad_request for these refusals (not_found for a missing paper); ErrorCode has no BAD_REQUEST, so the refusal is 422 VALIDATION_ERROR (mapping awaits the LEAD decision, deviations log). Quota by role (BR-M13-06), counted per user per Malaysia calendar day from the stored user messages: `admin` tier `admin` 100 turns, `teacher` tier `guru` 30, every other role tier `pelajar` 10. When used >= limit: 429 body exactly `{"quota_exhausted": true}` and nothing is stored. `turns_remaining` = limit - (used + 1). Routing of the reply is deterministic string logic on the server (BR-M13-04), first match on the trimmed message, case-insensitive: starts with "Tolong mark karangan ini menggunakan rubric " = `mark_essay` (stores an essay marking); contains "rph" = RPH tool (stores an RPH when subject and level are found); contains "latihan" or "soalan" = practice reply; otherwise the general reply. `tool_hops` is 1 when the turn ran mark_essay, saved an RPH or returned practice questions, else 0. With the mock AI provider `tokens.in = 120 + ceil(codepoints(message) / 4)` and `tokens.out = ceil(codepoints(reply) / 4)`. AI: the reply, marks and RPH text come from the mock provider or, later, the BE-36 adapter (redaction, rate limit, cost log, budget); this route calls no AI vendor. PDPA: the user is often a minor. The message and reply are personal data: never logged, `Cache-Control: no-store`, sent to a provider only after redaction. The contract makes no statement that content is not used to train models (open question). The CSRF header is checked (403 CSRF_INVALID, standard envelope).

post.description: Card BE-38. Roles (D40a): Guru (`teacher`) on the batches they own, Admin Pusat (`admin`) on all. Admin Sekolah, PPD and every other role get 403. Idempotent per batch: a new request enqueues a run (202); a request while a run is queued or running returns that run (202); a request after a succeeded run returns it unchanged (200, no new items, no cost). After a failed run the same request retries and creates no duplicate items. When BE-36 reports the monthly budget exhausted the run stays `queued` with `reason.code` AI_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and resumes when the cap is raised (202, not an error). A file whose hash was already imported by ANOTHER finished batch is refused before any provider call: 409 CONFLICT "Kertas sama sudah diimport"; `details.batchId` names the earlier batch ONLY when that batch is in the scope of the caller (a Guru is never told about another teacher batch), otherwise `details` is omitted and the message is the same. A batch that cannot be extracted yet (no stored file, a file still being processed, a manual batch) is 409 CONFLICT "Kumpulan ini belum boleh diekstrak: tiada fail, atau fail masih diproses." [PROPOSED]. The request body is empty; the pages come from the stored batch.

post.summary: Accept an item: create a Draf question
post.description: Card BE-38 (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC9). Roles (D40a): Guru (`teacher`) on the batches they own, Admin Pusat (`admin`) on all. Admin Sekolah, PPD and every other role get 403. Only an authenticated human reviewer can call it; the AI service cannot. Runs the quality gate for this item: every per-question rule of the prototype validateBatch (low fields confirmed, marks equal the sum of the part marks, ...), plus the unit being in the curriculum list and the item's stimulus having alt text and a stored figure (INTAKE_ACCEPT_BLOCKING_RULES). Batch-level rules (source, copyright, empty batch, group order) and an open exact or near duplicate entry do NOT block accept; BE-10 submit enforces them. On failure 422 VALIDATION_ERROR with `details.issues`. An item in state `duplicate` (a person linked it) is refused: 409 "Item ini ditandakan sebagai pendua. Pilih Bukan pendua dahulu untuk menerimanya." [PROPOSED]; a rejected item: 409 "Item ini sudah diterima atau ditolak dan tidak boleh disunting."; an accepted item: 409 "Item ini sudah diterima.". Only the first accepted item of a stimulus group snapshots the stimulus into the bank; later ones join that group. On success the server creates a question through QuestionsService with status `draft` (wire code, D54a) and provenance, and stores its id and version on the item (`question`). Submit, approve and publish are the BE-10 endpoints.
